proposal.title: IBM Cloud read-only drift & correction-planning sketch
proposal.body: End-to-end flow: synthetic inventory → read-only collector → versioned snapshot → drift + policy checks → watsonx.ai correction proposal → Schematics plan-only → reviewable diff → human approval, with Activity Tracker/Cloud Logs audit. No apply/delete path exists; credentials are read-only and held in Secrets Manager. Assumptions: region, account, IBM plans and model access are unselected and unverified; the inventory is synthetic; the model is mocked in local tests. Native Terraform generation for these IBM components is not yet available, so engineering is still needed.

data.description: Holds the API key for a read-only Service ID (Viewer/Reader roles only). The system never asks for broader credentials or creates them on its own.

data.label: Inventory collector
data.description: Read-only job that normalises the inventory into a snapshot. Locally it reads the synthetic fixture. Against a real account it would call read-only Resource Controller/Global Search APIs.

data.label: Snapshot & baseline store
data.description: Versioned bucket holding inventory snapshots, the desired-state baseline, plans and diffs. No delete path is granted to the pipeline.

data.label: Drift detector
data.description: Deterministic comparison of the latest snapshot with the baseline. Emits a list of drift findings.

data.label: Policy checks
data.description: Evaluates the snapshot against policy rules, e.g. encryption, public access and tags. Results are deterministic and independent of the model.
data.service: IBM Cloud Code Engine (OPA policy-as-code); IBM Cloud Security and Compliance Center for real accounts

data.label: Correction planner
data.description: Turns drift and policy findings into a proposed Terraform change with an explanation. Its output is untrusted until it passes the policy checks again. Locally a scripted mock answers, which proves nothing about real model quality.

data.label: Plan generator (plan only)
data.description: Runs terraform plan on the proposed change in a Schematics workspace. The pipeline identity is not granted apply or destroy actions.

data.label: Diff review & approval
data.description: Shows the plan diff, findings and rationale. The reviewer approves or rejects, and the decision is recorded. Approval does not trigger an apply in this scope.
data.service: IBM Cloud Code Engine (app) + IBM Cloud App ID sign-in

data.label: Audit trail
data.description: Records every collection, check, model call, plan and approval decision with actor and timestamp.
data.service: IBM Cloud Activity Tracker Event Routing + IBM Cloud Logs

Act as a patient architecture consultant and teacher. Start with what the evidence shows is working, explain the most important remaining issue in plain language, and help the user make progress. Do not just recite a checklist or demand that a junior developer repair product internals. Offer a concrete supported correction when possible; otherwise ask one focused question and explain why its answer matters. Help improve this architecture from its current emulation results. Diagnose the first actionable finding. Propose a minimal supported architecture correction only when requirements already justify it; otherwise ask one precise question.
Preserve all required components, existing systems, IDs, established service choices, access boundaries and requirements. Never clear unfinished-work gates, remove workload scope, weaken tests or invent successful validation. A graph proposal cannot repair generator/runtime source or an emulator defect: identify that as product engineering work with a reproducer. Model output is not test evidence. A local emulation pass is not a cloud plan or deployment. After an applied correction, rerun emulation on the new artifact; do not reuse this result. response.message: The emulation found nothing broken (zero failures), and the flow from inventory to plan to approval to audit is fully connected. It's blocked because no supported generator exists for these IBM components yet: there's no typed contract for Code Engine jobs, Secrets Manager, Schematics plan-only or watsonx.ai, and the two existing references (reviewer, synthetic inventory) need a reference plan. Swapping in a contract that is supported, like plain IBM Cloud Object Storage, would shrink the app down to storage, so I'm leaving the board as it is. The real fix is product engineering: native IBM implementations for these components, using this artifact (a3791d01…) as the reproducer. Until then the "correct" state for drift is still undecided, and the correction planner's output needs a defined re-check before review. When we look for drift, what should count as the correct state: Terraform code in a Git repo, a written policy set, or a known-good inventory snapshot?
